title: What the Hair Could Tell Us — Early Iron Age Tunnug 1 Cannabis Burial, Hair-Shaft CBN LC-HRMS/MS vs. Environmental Transfer, Human CB1-Gi1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9ERX) & Hallstatt Radiocarbon

teenKit.tldr: When archaeologists found a 2,800-year-old Siberian burial with cannabis seeds and a human hair braid, they had to use advanced chemistry to figure out if the person actually used the drug or just sat near it. This solves a high-stakes forensic cold case bridging ancient history and molecular biology.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that the flashy objects we dig up from the past don't always mean what our brain's love for a good story wants them to mean, teaching us how hard science strips away human bias.
keyTakeaways: Finding psychoactive plants next to ancient remains doesn't automatically mean the deceased consumed them, as environmental transfer and smoke can leave misleading traces.
Advanced analytical tools like LC-HRMS/MS let scientists detect specific molecular markers like cannabinol (CBN) directly trapped inside preserved human hair.
Structural biology uses tech like cryo-electron microscopy to show us down to the atomic level how ancient plant compounds physically lock into human cellular receptors.

vocab.meaning: The forensic science of detecting poisons, drugs, and chemicals in ancient human remains and artifacts.
A heavy-duty laboratory technique that separates and measures chemical compounds down to microscopic quantities.
A high-tech imaging method that freezes biological molecules to take hyper-detailed pictures of them at the atomic scale.
A mathematical correction method used to turn raw radioactive carbon breakdown data into precise historical calendar dates.

quiz.question: Why can't archaeologists automatically assume someone was high just because cannabis seeds were found in their grave?
options: The seeds might have been fake.
Chemicals can transfer from the environment or smoke without the person actually ingesting them.
quiz.explanation: Just like passive smoke today, external contamination can leave physical traces on hair and artifacts without internal consumption.

quiz.question: What does LC-HRMS/MS help scientists do in a case like Tunnug 1?
options: Build a 3D model of an ancient village
Accurately separate and detect chemical traces like CBN inside ancient hair samples
quiz.explanation: This advanced analytical chemistry technique is precise enough to hunt down specific drug metabolites and degradation products in tiny biological samples.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of structural biology tools like PDB 9ERX in this research context?
options: To map out the exact atomic interaction between cannabis compounds and human brain receptors
To dig up frozen Siberian soil without damaging hair
To calculate the exact year a burial mound was built
quiz.explanation: Cryo-EM structures show the physical lock-and-key fit of how these chemical compounds interact with our nervous system at a cellular level.
